title: Seeing is believing: in vivo functional real-time imaging of transplanted islets using positron emission tomography \(PET)
protocol: Anesthetize male C57BL/6 (8 - 12 week old) mice with intraperitoneal injection of pentobarbital (30 - 40 mg/kg).
Make a midline skin incision in the abdomen under the rib cage after the animal is fully anesthetized.
Clamp the common bile duct and distend the pancreas by injecting 2 - 3 ml of collagenase (1000 U/ml) in Hanks' Balanced Salt Solution through the pancreatic duct with a 30G needle.
Remove the pancreas and euthanize the donor mouse appropriately.
Place the pancreas in a 50 mL tube containing 2 - 3 mL of collagenase (1000 U/ml) in HBSS for 13-min in a water bath at 37°C.
Stop the digestion by adding 15 mL of cold HBSS II.
Shake the tubes by hand to disrupt the pancreas.
Centrifuge at 1200 rpm for 1 min and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with cold HBSS II.
Repeat steps centrifuging and resuspending twice more.
Resuspend resulting pellets in RPMI 1640 Solution B.
Pour resuspended solution onto a pre-wetted 70 μm nylon mesh cell strainer.
Wash the filter with RPMI 1640 Solution B.
Rinse the captured islets into a petri-dish with RPMI 1640 Solution A.
Repeat steps for the second mouse.
Hand-pick individual islets under the microscope.
Transfer picked islets to fresh RPMI 1640 medium A.
Culture islets in RPMI 1640 medium A.
Expose islets to 250 multiplicity of infection purified recombinant adenoviruses expressing HSV1-sr39tk for 2 h at 37°C.
Centrifuge the islets at 1200 rpm for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with HBSS.
Repeat centrifugation and resuspension steps twice.
Re-culture islets in RPMI 1640 Solution A.
Induce general anesthesia of male C57BL/6 mice by isoflurane inhalation.
Place the anesthetized mouse on a heating pad.
Shave and wash the skin with 70% Ethanol over the surgery site.
Perform a lombotomy to expose the right kidney.
Make a breach in the kidney capsule.
Introduce a polyethylene catheter through the breach.
Advance the catheter into the subcapsular space to the opposite pole of the kidney.
Slowly inject the islets through the catheter, allowing them to spread at the pole.
Retrieve the catheter and cauterize the opening.
Reposition the kidney.
Close the musculo-peritoneal layer with #5.0 absorbable suture in an interrupted pattern.
Close the skin incision with #5.0 absorbable suture in an interrupted pattern.
Wash the surgical site again with providine solution for aseptic preparation.
Repeat steps 24 to 32 for the surgery of the left kidney.
Induce general anesthesia of male C57BL/6 (8 - 12 week old) mice by isoflurane inhalation.
Place the mouse on a heating pad once fully anesthetized.
Shave and wash the skin with 70% Ethanol over the surgery site.
Make a midline skin incision in the abdomen under the rib cage.
Carefully raise the musculo-peritoneal layer to avoid damage to the bowel.
Make an incision in the peritoneal wall directly beneath the cutaneous incision.
Move the intestine to the right using cotton-tipped applicators, and expose the hepatic portal vein.
Slowly inject the islets (in a standard 200 μl volume) into the hepatic portal vein using an insulin syringe (29 1/2").
Press the surgifoam against the injection site with a cotton-tipped applicator.
Retrieve the syringe carefully from the portal vein simultaneously.
Apply surgifoam to completely stop the bleeding, then remove.
Close the musculo-peritoneal layer with #5.0 absorbable suture in an interrupted pattern, taking care to avoid perforation of the underlying bowel.
Close the skin incision with #5.0 absorbable sutures in an interrupted pattern.
Wash the surgical site again with providine solution for aseptic preparation.
Dissolve Kryptofix 222 (12 mg) and K₂CO₃ (3 mg) in 0.4 mL of water:acetonitrile 1:3.
Dissolve FHBG precursor (1.5 mg) in 0.4 mL of acetonitrile:DMSO 1:1.
Place a vial with [¹⁸F]F-/¹⁸O-water (200-300 mCi, from 15 min cyclotron target irradiation) into a hot cell and connect addition and transfer lines.
Push air through the addition line to transfer ¹⁸O-water into a water recovery vial.
Connect anion exchange resin to the reaction vessel.
Pass a solution of K₂CO₃/Kryptofix 222 through the addition line followed by a gentle flow of helium.
Connect a second addition line to the reaction vessel with a needle going to the vessel bottom and place the vessel in an oil bath to dry liquid with a gentle stream of helium.
Addition of acetonitrile (3 × 0.33 mL) removes traces of water, followed by evaporation each time.
Add the solution of precursor (Tosyl-FHBG) via the addition line.
Place the vessel into an oil bath and heat for 10 min at 100°C.
Put reaction vessel back in the nest, connect went and addition line. Add 0.3 mL of 2 M HCl.
Heat the vessel in the oil bath for 5 min.
Put reaction vessel back in the nest, connect went and addition line, add 3 mL of saturated sodium tetraborate and introduce a gentle flow of helium to mix the solution. Turn off helium flow.
Remove went line, connect a transfer line. Slowly transfer half of the reaction vessel content into the injector loop and perform injection.
Collect [¹⁸F]FHBG radiopeak into the rotary evaporator.
Evaporate collected liquid in the rotary evaporator.
Stop evaporator rotation.
Add saline to the rotary evaporator.
Bring rotary evaporator to ambient pressure.
Turn on rotation for a few seconds.
Transfer the solution of [18F]FHBG into the product vial.
Weigh the product vial.
Count the radioactivity in the product vial.
Withdraw 0.2 - 0.3 mL QC sample from the vial.
Inject 10 μL of the QC sample on analytical HPLC.
Transfer resulting [18F]FHBG to PET suite for microPET studies.
Transport islet-transplanted mice to the PET suite.
Induce general anesthesia with isoflurane inhalation in a closed container.
Place the mice on the scanner bed in a prone position.
Fit a nose cone over the face of the mice to maintain isoflurane anesthesia.
Place an intravenous catheter (27G butterfly) in the tail vein.
Slowly drip saline to maintain catheter patency.
Draw 100 μCi of \[^{18}\]F-FHBG.
Top up the dose with sterile saline to a constant injection volume of 0.5 mL.
Inject the \[^{18}\]F-FHBG solution through the tail vein over 20-30 seconds.
Start list mode scanning for 1 hour following tracer injection.
Obtain a 15-minute attenuation scan immediately after the initial scan.
Remove the intravenous line and nose cone, then monitor the mouse until it is fully awake.
Determine the framing sequence for the list mode data (6 - 30 sec, 2 - 1 min, 5 - 5 min, and 4 - 7.5 min) and reconstruct using filtered back projection with ASIPro software.
Reconstruct a single time frame from 30-60 minutes post-injection using the three-dimensional iterative maximum a posteriori algorithm to improve organ identification and accuracy of ROI positioning.
Determine the 2-3 slices where the kidney or liver is best visualized.
Draw circular ROIs (of the same size in all slices) on the kidney or liver areas of the MAP image.
Reposition the ROIs on the corresponding slices of the kinetically reconstructed data to generate time activity curves for each region.
Convert the counts/pixel/minute obtained from the ROI to counts/ml/minute using the calibration constant.
Convert the ROI counts/ml/minute to counts/g/minute, assuming a tissue density of 1g/ml.
Divide the converted counts by the injected dose (100 μCi) to generate TACs as percentage injected dose of [18F]FHBG retained in the kidney or liver.
